title: Prioritization gateway for custom dashboard & export requests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We continue to receive a high volume of console and reporting requests from enterprise customers that span simple usage queries to large encrypted exports and tenant-aware dashboards. Current intake is ad-hoc (email/Slack/Forms) and lacks consistent SLAs or routing, which causes missed expectations, scope creep, and engineering context-switching.

Goal: Create a structured prioritization gateway that routes incoming console/reporting asks into three operational lanes (self-serve, standard SLA, white-glove) based on explicit criteria and an automated scoring model. The gateway should capture essential metadata, surface cost/complexity estimates to customers, and generate a Linear ticket with lane assignment and required attachments for engineering/design review.

Scope: Intake form + backend scoring + routing rules + minimal console UI for request status. Integrations: Confluence PRD link, GitHub PR creation template, Slack notifications to #console-ops. Out-of-scope: full implementation of export plumbing; those are separate implementation tickets.

Proposed approach: 1) Design an intake schema capturing tenant size, data sensitivity, export frequency, expected row/byte counts, encryption requirement, and desired SLA. 2) Build a lightweight scoring service that maps attributes to lanes and a preliminary cost multiplier (est token/GB estimate). 3) Add gating logic: encrypted or >10TB or requiring dedicated capacity => white-glove; enterprise customers requesting SLA/retention >90 days => standard/white-glove; simple dashboard filters/one-off CSVs => self-serve. 4) Create templates and checklists per lane to ensure engineering/design have required artifacts before work begins. 5) Instrument metrics (time-to-assign, lead time by lane, customer satisfaction).

Acceptance criteria: - Intake form created and published (Confluence + Console link). - Automated scoring returns consistent lane assignment for a sample set of 40 historical requests (>=90% agreement with PM triage). - New Linear tickets created with lane tag and required attachments checklist. - Console UI shows request status and estimated cost range for self-serve/standard lanes. - Pilot with 3 enterprise customers for 4 weeks and SLA adherence >=90%.

Constraints & risk: - Cost estimation accuracy depends on telemetry that is partially incomplete for older tenants. Work with analytics team to backfill key metrics. - Encryption/KMS requirements may force Private deployment conversations; security review required for white-glove flows. - Need legal signoff for customer data exports and retention rules.

Stakeholders: PM (Maya Chen), Eng leads (SRE: Oliver Park, Backend: Priya Rao), Design: Luca Moretti, Security: Hannah Riley, Solutions/SE: Jonas Alvarez.

Success metrics: - Reduce engineering triage time by 45% for console/reporting asks. - Decrease scope-change tickets post-acceptance by 60%. - 75% of new requests resolved via self-serve or standard lanes (no white-glove) within first quarter after rollout.
